Commander night at Alex's house on Moraga Way in Orinda, Friday 28 August. Three-player pod: me, Alex, Stuart. Four games across the night, one deck each game, and this was game one of four.

Mulliganed into a hand that looked good and was structurally dead: a clean land base, one-drop instants and sorceries, Crimson Wisps and Storm-Kiln Artist. Zero goblins. So I had the entire storm-and-copy half of the engine in hand and nothing to multiply through. The deck fizzled.

The lesson is about the mulligan gate, and I got it wrong in the moment because the hand read as strong. The gate is GOBLIN PRESENCE, not cantrip density. A hand full of cantrips and a copy engine with no body to target is a hand that does nothing, however good the individual cards look. I should have shipped it.

No changes to the deck. This was a bad draw and a bad keep, not a deck problem. It stays pinned at v1.0.0, precon as printed.

Game 1 of three at Oliver's, five-player pod: Sean, Oliver, Tom, Alex, Ryan.

Kept an opener of three basics, a utility land (enters tapped unless you control
three basics; makes a 1/1 dwarf if it comes in untapped) and Krenko, Mob Boss.
Liked the hand at the time.

It had land and a value engine and NO SMALL GOBLINS — the actual fuel for the
deck. The instants and sorceries were there but all expensive, so the cantrip
half never turned over. The engine never assembled.

Table was three mono-red decks: Oliver on Krenko doing token-and-ping, Tom on
Purphoros doing the same, plus more red besides. The red density took the game
over. Oliver killed the table on turn five off Krenko tokens and pings.

Loss.

The lesson I want to keep: GOBLIN PRESENCE GATES THE MULLIGAN, not cantrip
density. Cheap goblin bodies are non-negotiable for this deck to function, and
I kept a hand that had none.

## Game 2: Zeta, Hedron Collider (win)

Sean won on the turn after Alex killed Ryan: Empty the Warrens, Impact Tremors, 15 mana and a 20-plus goblin board, all +3/+2, swung for lethal at Alex. Sean was at 23 life.

**Table:** Sean on Zeta (Goblin Storm), Alex on his R/G fight deck (bracket 3), Ryan on T'Vol, his best deck.

**Deck state**

- Targeted at bracket 3. The two-card infinite combo (Glimpse the Impossible plus another piece) was taken out; with it in, the deck rated bracket 4.
- Built around Zeta's ability: get Zeta out, get creatures out, then cast things.
- New cards that mattered tonight: Deflecting Swat, a new artifact-removal spell, and a new land (pay two, tap, get one mana of any color) that fits a mono-red deck.

**How the game went**

1. Ryan built an engine with T'Vol, Gravecrawler and Phyrexian Altar: Gravecrawler keeps returning, T'Vol makes a Zombie Druid each time, and the Altar turns Druids into mana. The board filled with Zombie Druids, enough to swing lethal at both opponents. Needing the Altar was the weak point.
2. Alex fought Zeta. Sean cast Deflecting Swat and redirected the fight to a 1/1 goblin, losing one goblin instead of the commander.
3. Alex stopped Ryan's engine. Alex thought the Altar had to go, so Sean cast the new artifact-removal spell and destroyed it. Ryan told Sean he was playing kingmaker; Sean's answer was that without removing the Altar the game was over, so removing it was the better chance.
4. Alex killed Ryan and hit Sean for 17 (40 to 23).
5. Sean's turn: cantripped into Empty the Warrens for about 10 goblins. Impact Tremors was already on the board and dealt 10 to each opponent. The new land helped reach 15 mana, then Sean drew about 15 cards and chained spells, giving haste, trample and +3/+2 to a 20-plus goblin board.
6. Swung for lethal at Alex. No response.

**Order check:** the Impact Tremors damage timing relative to Ryan's death was stated loosely. Sean said it happened before the final turn.

## Table politics and vibe

Sean teamed up with Ryan early in game 2, dropped the alliance when Ryan's engine went infinite-ish, and let Alex take Ryan out. He had to win that turn: if Alex lived, Sean was dead on the next one.

- Piloting Zeta felt like walking a tightrope and threading a needle. Lots of options, one correct sequence, big payoff when it lands.
- Sean thinks this is how Alex and Oliver feel with their decks all the time.
- Mood: stoked. Deflecting Swat gets a "great card, glad it's in the deck" mark, and the new any-color land is a perfect fit for mono-red.

## Lessons and deck follow-ups

| Deck | Lesson | Follow-up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sharknado | Opener had lands and ramp but no payoffs; the mulligan call is in question. Holding commanders for a wheel cost tempo when no wheel came. | Find a way to cheat out or ramp into both commanders sooner. Look at wheel count and the discard-a-card drag. |
| Sharknado vs. Alex's warp deck | Warp turns outpace Sharknado. | Work out an answer to the warp deck. |
| Zeta (Goblin Storm) | Sequencing and the right answers at the right time won it. Deflecting Swat saved the commander and the new artifact removal broke Ryan's engine. | None. The bracket 3 tune is working. |

Pilot's Notes — Tue Nov 10, 2026, Oliver's house
Pod: Sean, Oliver, Tom, Ryan (4-player). Bracket: 3. Record on the night: 0–3. Decks piloted: Goblin Storm (Zada) ×2, Shabraz, the Sky Shark ×1.

Table context
• Tom: Purphoros (mono-red ETB pings). Oliver: Balin (token maker; Krenko in game 3). Ryan: Tiny Bones (shared graveyard / steal).
• Pre-game talk was precons / bracket 2. Sean has no bracket 2 deck, so brought his lowest-power bracket 3 (Goblin Storm). Opponents' bracket 3 decks are highly optimized and aim to win around turn four.
• Games were very fast: game 1 ran about 30 minutes.

Game 1 — Goblin Storm (loss)
What happened
• Tom: turn-one Sol Ring → four mana turn two → Purphoros turn two, pinging every creature ETB.
• Game effectively over by turn four. Sean never cast Zada.
• Late: Oliver played The One Ring for protection; Tom ran out of gas. Winner not recorded (not Sean).
Assessment
• Should have mulliganed the opening hand.
• Turn-two Purphoros is not beatable from this deck's seat without early interaction. The counterplay is upstream: deny the Sol Ring (see game 2).
• Purphoros's downside — runs out of steam if it doesn't close — only matters if the table survives the first four turns.

Goblin Storm — deck feedback (future feature branch; do not iterate now)
Where it stands
• Against the B team (Steven, Stuart, David): great, fun, assembles turn 4–5, in position to win turn 6–7 when it pops off. Nothing wrong with the deck at that tier.
• Against the Oliver/Tom table: the clock is one to two turns too slow. A tier mismatch, not a deck defect.
Two levers — pick one direction
• Wide before Zada. Zada on turn four is fine if turns 1–3 build a wide goblin board. Needs more token makers / more cheap goblins. Recently added lands that tap for mana per goblin (naming goblins) support this.
• Zada faster. More rocks, dorks, or treasure to land Zada turn two or three, then accelerate off her (draw, tokens).
• Possibly also a draw/consistency problem — flag for measurement rather than assume.
Mulligan heuristic (proposed, matches the split)
• Keep if the hand either (a) makes many goblin tokens before Zada, or (b) lands Zada fast and has a payoff to accelerate off her. Ship hands with neither — including good-land, cantrip-heavy hands (consistent with Aug 28 and Sep 1 lessons).
Open note
• Krenko is in the list and almost never shows up. Sample size is small — more at-bats before drawing conclusions.
• Abrade earns its slot: removing a turn-one Sol Ring was the single most impactful play of the night.

Cross-game piloting lessons
• Threat removal beats tempo. Same pattern as Sep 2026 notes (Ur Dragon telegraphing, Edgar leaving Elspeth exposed): preferring own momentum over removing the obvious table threat. Rule: when the whole table names the threat and only you can answer it, answer it.
• Kill-on-sight list: Purphoros (Tom), Krenko (Oliver).
• Deny the Sol Ring opener. Early artifact removal is a legitimate tempo play against this pod; expect salt, do it anyway.
• Enchantment removal should be a standing slot audit across decks.
• Tier context: Oliver/Tom table bracket 3 ≈ optimized, turn-four clock; B-team (Steven, Stuart, David) bracket 3 ≈ turn 6–7 clock.

All figures are from Sean's verbal recap on Nov 11, 2026; turn counts and damage totals are approximate.

Game 2 — Goblin Storm, run-back, same decks (loss)
What happened
• Tom opened Sol Ring again. Sean removed it with Abrade (new addition). Tom was salty; without it, Purphoros lands turn two again.
• Purphoros still arrived, later. Oliver ran his Balin token line. Sean and Ryan middled with thin boards.
• Sean assembled the engine: Zada out, Storm-Kiln Artist out, a pile of treasure, and one of the new card-draw spells used to dig.
• Took roughly 10 then 12 ping damage per cycle plus constant attacks; the small goblins needed to copy spells kept dying. Lost on the clock.
Assessment
• Engine assembly worked. Survival did not. The deck had no way to stop the ping damage once Purphoros resolved.
• Artifact removal in red is worth the slot — Abrade came in exactly when needed.
• New card-draw additions helped.
